Synopsis:
UK farming organisations and animal health experts are urging a ban on Brazilian meat imports over antibiotic resistance (AMR) concerns. The EU is enacting such a ban imminently, but post-Brexit UK is not obliged to follow. Brazilian meat imports to the UK have grown significantly since Brexit (£3bn→£5bn), and with the EU market closing, trade diversion toward the UK is a key risk. Food safety, regulatory divergence from the EU, and Northern Ireland's unique post-Brexit status further complicate the picture.
